name: Epinephrine
route_note: IM auto-injector or nasal spray for anaphylaxis; IV or intraosseous in cardiac arrest and shock; nebulised for croup; combined with local anaesthetics
originator: Isolated by Jokichi Takamine (marketed by Parke-Davis)

discovery.note: Crystallised from adrenal glands; the hormone was also studied by John Jacob Abel and Napoleon Cybulski; first synthesised in 1904 by Friedrich Stolz and Henry Dakin. Parke, Davis & Co. trademarked and sold the purified extract as Adrenalin from 1901, before drug regulation.

tagline: First-line emergency treatment for anaphylaxis and a key drug in cardiac arrest
summary: Epinephrine (adrenaline) is the adrenal medullary hormone and neurotransmitter, used as a drug since the early 1900s. It is the first-line treatment for anaphylaxis, given intramuscularly or nasally, and is used intravenously in cardiac arrest and shock.
mechanism: Epinephrine stimulates alpha1 receptors, causing vasoconstriction that raises blood pressure and reduces mucosal oedema, and beta1 receptors, increasing heart rate and contractility.

Through beta2 receptors it relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and inhibits mediator release from mast cells and basophils. This combination reverses the hypotension, airway swelling and bronchospasm of anaphylaxis.
uses: Prolonging local anaesthesia and reducing bleeding

history.title: Isolation
history.detail: Jokichi Takamine isolates crystalline adrenaline; Parke-Davis markets it as Adrenalin.

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Friedrich Stolz and Henry Dakin independently synthesise epinephrine, the first hormone made synthetically.

history.title: EpiPen approved
history.detail: FDA approves the EpiPen auto-injector for anaphylaxis, adapted from military auto-injector technology.

history.title: EpiPen pricing controversy
history.detail: Steep US list-price rises for EpiPen prompt congressional hearings.

history.title: First generic EpiPen
history.detail: FDA approves Teva's generic version of EpiPen.

history.title: Nasal spray
history.detail: FDA approves neffy, the first needle-free epinephrine nasal spray for anaphylaxis; EU approves it as EURneffy.

pk.metabolism: COMT and MAO in liver, nerve endings and other tissues
pk.excretion: Urine as metanephrine and vanillylmandelic acid

serious: Severe hypertension and cerebral haemorrhage (overdose or IV bolus error)
Tissue necrosis after accidental injection into fingers or extravasation

facts: Adrenalin was among the first hormones isolated in pure form and the first to be chemically synthesised.
'Adrenaline' is the INN and the usual name in Europe; 'epinephrine' is the US adopted name.
